customer_jane: Hey team — hitting the rerank endpoint and seeing very odd numbers in `scores` (examples: -12.3, 0.42, 2.1). Are these probabilities? Our UI expects 0..1. Request id: req-01AYZ.
support_amy: Thanks @customer_jane — quick clarifying q: are you calling /v1/rerank with a batch of candidate lists or single-list calls? Also can you paste the raw JSON response (or a redacted snippet)? :thinking_face:
customer_jane: Single candidate list per request, payload small. Here's redacted response (only "candidates" and "scores"): ```json
{"candidates": ["docA","docB","docC"], "scores": [-12.345, 0.421, 2.103]}
```
support_amy: That helps. Short answer: what you're seeing are raw logits (model scoring space), not normalized probabilities. Negative values are normal for logits. To display probabilities, apply softmax across the candidates. Ordering is what matters for ranking (higher -> better).
ml_rohan: Adding: logits aren't bounded to [0,1], they can be negative or >1. Softmax(x)_i = exp(x_i) / sum_j exp(x_j). Example: given [-12.345,0.421,2.103] the softmax will put almost all mass on 2.103.
eng_carter: Filing a docs/update task, users frequently expect normalized scores. Ticket: INFR-542 — add explicit note and example for converting rerank logits -> probabilities, and add a `normalized_scores` output flag as a product idea.
support_amy: For repro, pls run this curl and paste the `x-request-id` if you still see anomalies: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"how to bake bread","candidates":["docA","docB","docC"]}' | jq .
```
customer_jane: Got it — x-request-id: req-01AYZ (same as above). Also curious if batching/padding could cause large negative values? We do server-side pooling of requests.
ml_rohan: Good question — padding itself shouldn't change relative logits for real candidates, but if you're concatenating candidates into a single sequence and truncation/prefixing differs across candidates, you might see artifacts. Also quantization/float precision on older GPU backends can amplify extreme logits if there's a bug.
eng_carter: We checked infra for req-01AYZ: request hit runtime pool node node-12, model variant r-rank-v2-q8_0. No obvious error logs.
support_amy: To be safe please try this local python snippet to convert to probabilities and confirm ordering looks correct before changing UI: ```python
import math
scores = [-12.345, 0.421, 2.103]
exp = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
sumexp = sum(exp)
probs = [e/sumexp for e in exp]
print(probs)
```
customer_jane: That produced [0.000002, 0.013, 0.987] — ok ordering is as expected. So UI can show probs.
ml_rohan: TL;DR: negatives are expected; treat rerank `scores` as logits. If you need stable probs for UX, softmax on the model-provided scores. We'll propose an API flag to return normalized scores server-side so clients don't have to.
support_amy: Follow-ups: 1) We'll update docs with clear language and code examples (INFR-542). 2) Eng will evaluate `normalized_scores` flag feasibility (INFR-543). 3) If you still see magnitude >100 or inconsistent ordering, paste x-request-id and we will open infra traces.
eng_carter: Note — also check that your client isn't accidentally combining scores from different requests (e.g., caching per-request candidate list id). That can look like non-normalized mixes.

support_amy: Closing loop — docs PR merged with softmax examples and note about logits. If anything else, re-open. :white_check_mark:
